I NTRODUCTION Pursuant to Article XII.1.b of the Convention, the Director General (DG) is the chief executive officer of the Agency, its legal representative, and has authority over the sites of the Agency. In that capacity, the DG has overall responsibility and is accountable for all health and safety risks (i) arising on ESA sites, and/or (ii) arising in the context of the Agency’s activities. The DG has thus responsibility for all persons 1 , irrespective of their status, who participate in the Agency’s activities or are physically present on its sites. What these responsibilities are, and how they should be discharged, depends upon the context, and includes risks to Staff members when on mission and teleworking. Employment is an opportunity for improving the physical and psychological health of manpower resources 2 . As well as benefiting individuals, the Agency will gain through health - related improvement in work performance and reduction in sickness absence. It is therefore in the interest of the Agency that risks to health and safety are identified and subject to constant reduction. Decisions that relate to the Agency’s activities will be motivat

POLICY It is the Agency’s policy to: - Keep as low as reasonably practicable all health and safety risks arising in the context of its activities. - Provide adequate resources to identify and manage risks and to improve continuously standards of health and safety. - Establish a working environment in which its manpower resources and any other individual on site performing temporary assignments (i.e., visiting scie

Maintain a monitoring regime to: - control health and safety risks. - monitor the status of health and safety management. - identify the root causes of incidents and instances of occupational illness. - keep track of changes to national health and safety legislation where ESA sites are located. - anticipate changes to the control of health and safety risks whether internal or external to the Agency. 3. SCOPE OF APPLICATION This policy applies to the activities of the Agency and to any person present on ESA sites (including manpower resources and visitors). It also applies to Staff members when on mission and during teleworking 3 . 4. Where appropriate, and when such assessment cannot reasonably be undertaken by the Agency itself, the Agency may rely on risk assessments undertaken by public authorities of the Memb er States or by other competent entities. 4.2 Reducing health and safety risks across the whole life cycle of an activity/asset For health and safety risks created by the Agency’s activities, the most effective way to reduce risk across the whole life cycle of an activity or asset is during its planning and design phases. Where this is not possible, then risk should be reduced according to a series of strategies in order of their effectiveness otherwise known as the safety precedence sequence. As F igure 1 below illustrates, risk reduction needs to be applied through the lifecycle of the activity/asset and should be reviewed when the activity/asset changes or if new information becomes available or due to changing circumstances. The lifecycle starts with planning and then design, followed by purchasing, fabrication, construction, operation, maintenance, and disposal. The Safety Precedence Sequence and the System Lifecycle 4.3 Promoting health and safety and providing appropriate means It is the duty of the manpower resources to make decisions and act in a way that promotes health and safety in the context of ESA’s activities by: - reducing the likelihood of harm occurring (to oneself and to others) and - advocating for s afe and healthy activities and workplaces. There are three main ways in which this duty is discharged: i. in the planning and conduct of work activities (for example with respect to the site, the operation’s specific location, on mission and during teleworking for staff members) ii. in the provision and maintenance of premises, plant, and equipment (sites, offices, laboratories, technical facilities, etc.) iii. in the provision of services from one department to another. To facilitate manpower resources duties, adequate resources will be provided to ensure that promotion of health and safety is given priority. The health and safety competence of the manpower resources is to be continuously developed. This will be specific to their function and within the fra mework of the Agency’s generic competency m

The state of conformance with the health and safety standards of local legislation shall be monitored and maintained on each site of the Agency. However, and b y way of exception to the above, the Director General may impose health and safety standards common to all sites of the Agency, if necessary. 4.5 Collaboration with National Authorities In keeping with the Convention, the Agency will cooperate with the competent authorities of Member States in matters of health and safety. 4.6 Keeping pace with Change Planned and unplanned changes can introduce new and unforeseen risks or increase existing risks to health and safety. This fact emphasises the importance of internal arrangements for active and reactive monitoring to foresee and detect changes allowing timely and appropriate review of the Agency’s activities. This also extends to the inv

the importance of internal arrangements for active and reactive monitoring to foresee and detect changes allowing timely and appropriate review of the Agency’s activities. This also extends to the investigation of unplanned events (i.e., incidents, accidents and near - mis ses…) as these provide an important trigger to identifying inadequately controlled risks. As well as vigilance to internal change, the Agency shall be alerted to changes in standards and approaches to health and safety in industry and society. External relationships and benchmarking are particularly important for proactively achieving this. Establishing and maintaining relationships with external associations is an important investment in the knowledge resources for the health and safety mission of the Ag ency. National enforcement agencies, such as labour inspectorates and fire departments, fall into this category. Monitoring and periodic reviews shall also provide an impetus to the continuous improvement of health and safety management in the Agency. 4.7 Involvement of the Staff representatives in health and safety matters Staff members, through their local SAC representatives for Health and Safety matters, have the right to: ESA/ADMIN/IPOL - HESA(20 22 )1 Page 6 - take part in discussions on all questions relating to health and safety in the workplace - make proposals to management about health and safety

Management accountability and commitment are key to establish a working environment in which the manpower resources recognise and assume responsibility for promoting health and safety at work. This includes measures that allow management to appraise and support Staff members in their efforts to deliver safe and healthy work, and measures such as those provided by the operation of health and safety committees at sites. The main approach is of positive, proactive, performance - based measurement. 4.9 Breach of health and safety rules Breaches of safety rules and/or wilful misuse of safety equipment by Staff Mem

The main approach is of positive, proactive, performance - based measurement. 4.9 Breach of health and safety rules Breaches of safety rules and/or wilful misuse of safety equipment by Staff Members ma y give rise to disciplinary action as detailed in the Agency’s Staff Regulations Rules and Instructions. The DG shall take appropriate steps towards contractors to ensure that contractor personnel comply with this Policy. In the event of a breach of safety rules and/or wilful misuse of safety equipment by contractor personnel, the Director General shall take appropriate measures. Similarly, in the event of a breach of safety rules and/or wilful misuse of safety equipment by other non - staff members, the Dire ctor General shall take appropriate measures. 4.10 Reporting of accidents and incidents Each member of the manpower resources is responsible for reporting incidents, accidents and near misses as soon as possible. ESA/ADMIN/IPOL - HESA(20 22 )1 Page 7 Reporting should be done locally via line managers or technical officers to a Health and Safety unit or officer or directly to a Health and Safety unit or officer (Establishment/Centre/Offices). 4.11 Purpose in the investigations of accidents and incidents Incidents and accidents are all oc currences arising out of, or in the course of, work that could or do result in injury and ill health. An “accident” does result in injury or ill health. Specifically: - Accident Injury is an adverse effect on someone’s physical condition. - Accident Ill Hea lth is adverse effect on someone's mental or cognitive condition. - Incident Near Miss (unsafe condition) is an incident where no injury and ill health occurs but has the potential to do so – including technical incidents that could have caused injury or saf ety issues. If a person is impacted, their line manager or technical officer must also be immediately informed of the incident/event that happened. The purpose of an investigation is to find out the relevant facts that led to the incident, accident or near miss, to learn lessons and implement relevant changes to ensure it will not recur. The investigation can be local or Corporate according to the criticality of the event. An investigation should identify points for improving safety within an Establishment/Centre/Office within a project or programme, and across the Agency. Where several activities are taking place together, the Agency must ensure that these activities are co - ordinated. 4.13 Fitting the work to the person, and being alert to individual differences in vulnerability The Agency shall be vigilant to the possible effects of individual differences to assumptions that are made in the design of work and workplaces, including emergency escape arrangements and guidelines for a healthy work environment. The design of workplaces, worksta tions, and work activities shall benefit from an approach that “fit the work to the person” rather than assuming the person will adapt. This principle of tailoring work to the individual shall also extend to the use of, and exposure to, chemicals, energies and environments that may pose a risk to health and safety. The Agency will consider the effects of individual variability (i.e. , age, gender, temporary or permanent changes to ability etc) on any exposure limit stated in authoritative published standards. 5. The Programme Directors, the Heads of Establishment, the Heads of Departments in charge of facilities management, personnel matters, and procurement will provide a detail ed report at least once a year to the Director General of the work carried out to implement this policy.
